note: After the revision by Constantino (1995), the original in English. The alate, the soldier (including the first-form soldier) and the large worker are described. The original also lists measurements of 13 large workers from 11 colonies (not all of them taken item by item here). The species is one of the type species of the genus described by Latreille (1804); the original records that part of the soldiers from Matto Grosso have less hair on the head.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The alate resembles S. dirus, S. cearensis, S. aculeosus, S. chaquimayensis and S. tanygnathus and is difficult to distinguish from some of them: S. dirus, S. cearensis and S. aculeosus have shorter hair on the head (S. aculeosus has a larger fontanelle and a different pronotum); S. tanygnathus has 21-segmented antennae; for S. chaquimayensis see the comparison under that species. This is a forest species, apparently very common in the Amazon region, its nest described by Emerson (1938).

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Compound eyes small, less than 1/4 of the head width; ocelli small; fontanelle round and of moderate size. Antennae 20-segmented. Anterolateral corners of the pronotum angular and with pointed processes; lateral margins slightly S-shaped, the anterior half nearly parallel. Wings short, the ends of the media and cubitus distinct. Head capsule with a few scattered setae; postclypeus with 6—8 setae.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule short to moderately elongate, sides converging forwards; posterior margin of the head rounded. Frontal tube projecting, or short and set in a small depression, its aperture usually not visible in dorsal view. Labrum short, length nearly equal to width; lateral corners about right-angled; median lobe short. Antennae 19 or 20-segmented. Postmentum not constricted. The morphology of the first-form soldier is also given (figs. 271—273); the original describes them separately.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Large worker: head capsule and postclypeus with many erect setae; fontanelle round and relatively small. Antennae 20-segmented. Thoracic spines well developed. Molar plate of the mandibles rather narrow, the basal notch slightly more than 90°. Hindgut similar to that of S. dirus, but the main prolongation of the mesenteron in the mixed segment is wider.
